correctness.rationale: For each orientation of the central edge, sink weights of leaf edges yield the closed identity. Factoring off (1+z)^2 proves the double root at -1. The positive-u sign comparisons establish the unique nonnegative-u root. For even b, one Descartes sign change gives one negative-u root. For odd b, the sign pattern bounds the count by two; an exact positive Bernstein certificate excludes all odd b<=13, while the rational H_13(6/5)>0 witness forces two simple roots for all odd b>=15. Endpoint limiting behavior follows from pointwise sign changes. Direct small-order enumeration and exact certificate checks passed.

value.rationale: Real-root locations and counts, rather than only orientation totals, are a motivated natural invariant following the recent acyclic sink-polynomial literature. A 19-vertex diameter-three tree is the first odd member whose sink polynomial gains two additional real zeros, and the phenomenon persists on all larger odd b. The exact non-monotone parity change and endpoint limits explain graph-root behavior outside existing claw-free hypotheses.
